01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

An early venture needs a repeatable way to identify and engage potential institutional partners. The first challenge was deciding where to focus.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Researched and prioritised 30+ K–12 and higher-education institutions by curriculum alignment, institution size and estimated willingness to invest. Built email outreach sequences, a partner-qualification rubric and pilot-proposal templates.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

Generated qualified leads and pilot conversations, with several discussions reaching proposal stage. In August 2025, exited after assessing that institutional willingness to pay and procurement constraints would not support sustainable unit economics.

IN THE DETAILS

Knowing when to stop

Institutional procurement emphasised price and compliance, limiting pricing power for a specialised learning product. The exit decision became a practical lesson in testing business viability before scaling commitment. It also informed the subsequent focus on operational-efficiency problems in healthcare.

THE TAKEAWAY

A proposal pipeline is useful evidence of interest. Sustainable willingness to pay is a separate question—and sometimes the most valuable decision is to stop.
